items.text: Canonical topology
\operatorname{Hom}(Y,Z)\to\textstyle\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i,Z)\ \text{injective: too weak (epimorphic family)}
Strictly epimorphic: the sheaf-like condition (equaliser) as well.

Finest topology on $C$ making representable functors sheaves: coverings = families strictly epimorphic universally (stable under base change). Not all strictly epimorphic families — they need not form a topology.
(SGA 4.) Representables are sheaves $\iff$ the topology is coarser than the canonical topology.
C\subset\widetilde C\ \subset\widehat C\quad\text{(then }C\to\widetilde C\text{ fully faithful)}
Then view $C$ inside $\widetilde C$: exactness there is as good as in sets. Direct limits in $C$: be careful that they are also direct limits in $\widetilde C$.
Look for criteria for direct limits to be universal and effective.
General case: $C\not\subset\widetilde C$. Define
\varepsilon_C\colon C\to\widetilde C,\qquad \varepsilon_C(X)=a(X)\quad(\text{associated sheaf of }X\in\widehat C)
\varepsilon_C\text{ fully faithful}\iff C\subset\widetilde C\iff\text{topology coarser than the canonical one}
Otherwise do not identify $C$ with its image.
Still: the image of $C$ in $\widetilde C$ is a generating subcategory.
F\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(\varepsilon_C X,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\widehat C}(X,F)=F(X)\quad\text{(jointly conservative)}
$C$ small $\Rightarrow$ $\widetilde C$ has small generators: a topos.
A topos as a site
$E$ a topos: take $C=E$ with the canonical topology. Epimorphic families are universally strictly epimorphic.
(X_i\to X)\ \text{covering}\iff\textstyle\coprod X_i\to X\ \text{epimorphism}
F\ \text{sheaf}\iff F\ \text{turns sums into products},\ \ F(X)\to F(X')\rightrightarrows F(X'\times_XX')\ \text{exact for epi }X'\to X
E\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\widetilde E\quad(\text{every sheaf is representable})
Of all ways to write a topos as $\widetilde C$, the best: take the whole topos (as all elements generate a group). So sites need not be small.
$U$-sites
Associated sheaf needs an inductive limit over a possibly too large set. $U$ = universe. A $U$-site:
(i) a $U$-category: $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)$ small.
(ii) a small subcategory $C_0$ that generates the site: every $X\in C$ has a covering $(X_i\to X)$ with all $X_i\in C_0$.
\widetilde C\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\widetilde{C_0}\quad(\text{restriction; }C_0\text{ with the induced topology})
So a $U$-site behaves as if small; the associated sheaf stays in the universe (comparison lemma).
Example of a non-small $U$-site: all schemes (or analytic spaces) over a ring with the étale or flat topology.
Topologies $=$ localisations
Two theorems that go together. $T$ a topology on $C$; $E_T=\widetilde C_T\subset\widehat C$ strictly full.
\text{(1)}\quad (X_i\to X)\ T\text{-covering}\iff (\varepsilon X_i\to\varepsilon X)\ \text{epimorphic in }\widetilde C
\varepsilon_C=a\circ\text{incl.}\ ,\quad a\dashv i\ (a\ \text{left adjoint of the inclusion})
R\subset X\ \text{sieve covering}\iff a(R)\to a(X)\ \text{isomorphism}
\text{(2)}\quad E\subset\widehat C\ \text{strictly full},\ i\colon E\to\widehat C\ \text{with left exact left adjoint }a\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists!\,T:\ E=\widetilde C_T
One-to-one: topologies on $C$ $\leftrightarrow$ such subcategories of $\widehat C$.
(a_T,i_T)\colon \widetilde C_T\to\widehat C\ \text{morphism of topoi, } i_T=f_*\ \text{fully faithful}
f\colon X\to Y,\ f_*\ \text{fully faithful}\iff \mathcal T_X=f^{-1}\mathcal T_Y\ \ (\text{sober: homeomorphism onto the image})
Embedding of topoi = $f_*$ fully faithful; subtopos. Topologies on $C$ $\leftrightarrow$ subtopoi of $\widehat C$.
$f_*$ fully faithful $\iff$ $f^*$ is a passage to fractions by a set of arrows.
Classifying topos of a structure: subtopoi = adding axioms. All ways of adding axioms to a type of structure $\leftrightarrow$ topologies on $C$.
\text{subtopoi of }\widetilde C_T\ \leftrightarrow\ \text{topologies }T'\text{ on }C\text{ finer than }T\ (\text{more coverings, fewer sheaves})
(Giraud.) Basic statement once topologies are varied systematically.
Further examples: quotient topoi (foliations); many exercises in SGA 4.
Comparison lemma
$C$ a site, $C_0\subset C$ full, with the induced topology (finest making the inclusion continuous).
\widetilde C\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\widetilde{C_0}\iff C_0\ \text{topologically generating (every object covered by objects of }C_0)
Generalises: a basis of open sets of a space $X$ gives the same sheaves.
F(X)=\ker\Bigl(\prod F(X_i)\rightrightarrows\prod F(X_{ij\alpha})\Bigr),\quad X_i,X_{ij\alpha}\in C_0
Many sites for one topos; what matters is the topos.
Characterisation of topoi (Giraud)
$E$ a $U$-category ($\operatorname{Hom}$ small). Equivalent:
(a) $E\simeq$ sheaves on a $U$-site; or on a small site stable under fibre products.
(b) a fully faithful $i\colon E\to\widehat C$ ($C$ small) with a left exact left adjoint $a$.
(c) exactness properties of $E$ plus a small generating family — the extra proof, not seen yet.
Corollary: all ways to realise $E$ by a site $C\subset E$ with topology coarser than the canonical one.
E\to\widehat C,\quad X\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(-,X)|_C
